messages:
alex: Taking primary for the 10:00-18:00 PT rotation. Leaving detailed handoff here so whoever picks this up has the quick checklist and emergency snippets.

maria: thanks — can pair for a 09:50 warm handoff? I'll run the smoke checks and verify dashboards.

alex: yes 09:50 works. Short checklist for incoming primary:
- confirm primary/secondary tags in the Ops Console (Routing -> Oncall)
- run the local smoke script: `./scripts/smoke-check --env prod`
- warm caches by hitting the top ~1% tenant traffic via `tools/warmup --targets top-tenants`
- confirm model versions pinned for your traffic slice

sam: can we add an item for KV-cache fallback pointer? yesterday's deploy showed cache thrash -> CPU spike.

alex: good call. adding explicit pointers below. Emergency runbooks and quick links:
- KV cache fallback runbook: https://redwood.company/runbooks/kv-cache-fallback
- Model routing & fallback: https://redwood.company/runbooks/model-routing-fallback
- Pager escalation matrix: https://redwood.company/runbooks/pager-escalation
- Ops quick CLI cheats: https://redwood.company/ops/cli-cheats

leah: drop the quick command snippets here too so they show up in search.

alex: snippets (copy/paste):
```
# scale down heavy workers immediately (fast mitigation)
kubectl scale deployment/inference-workers --replicas=1 -n prod

# temporarily route to smaller model variant via ops-api
curl -X POST "https://ops-api.internal/routes/fallback" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" -d '{"from":"gpt-3.8-large","to":"gpt-3.8-medium","reason":"latency spike"}'

# clear tenant prefix keys in Redis (use with caution)
redis-cli -h redis-prod -n 1 EVAL "return redis.call('DEL', KEYS[1])" 1 prefix:tenant:123

# turn on kv-cache-fallback flag (console path: Routing -> Flags)
# or via API:
curl -X POST "https://ops-api.internal/flags/kv-cache-fallback" -d '{"enabled":true}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN"
```

incident-bot: Pager alert: high p99 latency on text-gen (svc:text-gen). Pager: primary oncall: alex. Incident link: https://ops.incidents/INC-2026-4321

maria: got alert — starting smoke tests and checking recent deploys/logs.

sam: heads up — if KV is the culprit, enabling the kv-cache-fallback route buys us headroom while we investigate. Console path: Console -> Routing -> kv-cache-fallback.

alex: agree. if routing fallback is insufficient, use emergency model downgrade + scale ops. Emergency rollback command if needed: `gcloud run revisions rollback inference-prod --to-revision=rev-20260301`

leah: pointer for dashboards: use 1h and 15m windows to compare warmstart vs sustained load. Also check prefix cache hit ratio in the caching dashboard.

maria: smoke checks passing for basic endpoints. Latency improved slightly after enabling kv-cache-fallback. Leaving note in Ops ticket.

alex: adding operational notes to the incident ticket and handoff doc. Also: for any inherited pager, follow the quick triage flow in the pager runbook and tag the ticket with `primary-hand` so secondary knows you accepted it.

sam: I'll be primary backup from 14:00-18:00 if anything flares up.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-4321 acknowledged by alex at 2026-03-15T17:12:12Z

alex: final handoff items for the next incoming primary:
- replicate the warmup script output to the handoff note (ops/handovers/YYYYMMDD)
- if you see repeated KV evictions, follow the KV runbook step to enable prefix-scoped throttling before evicting keys
- escalate to infra oncall if CPU nodes exceed 85% for 5+ minutes

maria: noted. I've added a short postmortem checklist to: https://redwood.company/notes/handoff-warmstart

alex: closing this handoff thread — leaving the ticket in monitoring state and the runbook links above. Ping in #eng-oncall if anything regrows. :thumbsup:
